article.Citation: Davis AK, Renn E, Windham-Herman AM, Polanco M, Barsuglia JP. A Mixed Method Analysis of Persisting Effects Associated with Positive Outcomes Following Ibogaine Detoxification. Journal of Psychoactive Drugs. 2018.
article.Title: A Mixed Method Analysis of Persisting Effects Associated with Positive Outcomes Following Ibogaine Detoxification
article.GenderCategory: Male/Female binary breakdown reported: Male 70%, Female 30% (no non-binary/other category reported)

ae_events.Description: Psychological difficulty with commitment/adherence during the treatment week, self-reported as most challenging part of ibogaine detox (14 responders, 4 non-responders)
Health-related difficulty during treatment week (e.g., withdrawal from other substances such as cannabis), self-reported as most challenging part (13 responders, 6 non-responders)
Difficulty integrating the ibogaine experience into daily life, persisting weeks post-treatment; most frequently reported challenge overall (28 responders, 6 non-responders)
Post-treatment exhaustion/excessive need for sleep, self-reported as most challenging part of treatment (7 responders, 2 non-responders)
Post-treatment emotional distress described as 'uncomfortable and raw feelings' (11 responders, 1 non-responder)
Post-treatment restlessness, self-reported as most challenging part of ibogaine treatment (14 responders, 4 non-responders)

article.PosResult: Positive result: 81% of the 73 participants (59) were classified by the authors as treatment responders (never used opioids again or decreased use) on the study's own pre/post opioid-use outcome, and the title, abstract, and discussion explicitly report positive persisting psychosocial changes associated with ibogaine detoxification.
article.IsObservational: Secondary data analysis of a larger retrospective, anonymous web-based survey of patients who had already received one week of fee-for-service ibogaine detoxification at a residential clinic in Mexico (Davis et al. 2017 cohort). No randomization, no research-controlled dosing protocol; treatment was delivered as usual clinical care and surveyed retrospectively. Coded Y.
article.Corpus/Prefix: No substance/condition grouping prefix or corpus label given in the text beyond the Condition/Substance fields; coded '.'.
article.N: Final analyzed sample after exclusions (285 contacted -> 134 responded -> 88 in main outcome paper -> 73 completed persisting-effects measures) is 73; this is the denominator used for the demographic and quantitative PEQ analyses reported here.
article.AE_denominator: The article reports 'challenges' data as utterance counts from an open-ended survey question, broken out by responder (N=59) and non-responder (N=14) subgroup headers summing to 73, but does not state how many of the 73 actually answered the open-ended challenge question (one participant can contribute multiple utterances across multiple themes). Coded 'Not numbered' rather than assuming N=73 answered.
article.PctIndigenous: Table 1 reports only an aggregate 'Non-White/Other' ethnicity category (10%); no separate Indigenous breakout is given, so coded '.' rather than assuming it equals or is a subset with a specific value.
article.SafetyReported: This is not a formal clinical AE-surveillance study (no SAE log, no CTCAE grading, cardiac/medical monitoring is described only as routine protocol, not as a source of reported events). However, the article does explicitly and repeatedly characterize 'notable challenges' — psychological and health-related difficulties during treatment, and post-treatment integration difficulties — as a key finding (stated in the Abstract and analyzed via a dedicated open-ended question, Table 4). Given the instruction that understating harm is the cardinal error, this qualitative challenges reporting was treated as SafetyReported='Y' rather than treating the article as silent on safety.
article.AnyAEReported: Set Y on the same basis as SafetyReported — see above.
article.NumDistinctAEs: Coded as 6, corresponding to 6 during-/post-treatment challenge themes from Table 4 (Psychological, Health-related during treatment; Integration, Exhaustion/Fatigue, Emotional, Health-related post-treatment) that plausibly represent adverse/challenging effects of treatment. Excluded from this count: the 3 'pre-treatment' themes (occurred before ibogaine administration, not attributable to the drug/treatment), the 'Ibogaine Itself' during-treatment theme (exemplar quote 'the treatment itself' carries no distinguishable symptom content, too vague to describe as a distinct AE), and the post-treatment 'Staying off Opiates' and 'Cost-related' themes (relapse-risk and financial burden, not health/safety events).
article.NParticipantsWithAE: Table 4 gives utterance counts per theme, not participant-level counts, and one participant can contribute multiple utterances to multiple themes; no participant-level 'had >=1 AE' figure is reported, so coded '.'.
article.WorstSeverity: Equals Moderate, driven by AE03 (post-treatment integration difficulty), the only event graded above the Mild default — see that event's rationale below.

ae_events.Davis 2018_AE01: Under-specified qualitative theme ('being committed to the process') with no intervention/outcome/seriousness signal; defaulted to Mild per rubric and flagged SeverityIndeterminate=Y. Classified as challenging_experience (processing/adhering to the ibogaine treatment process) rather than a discrete clinical AE.
ae_events.Davis 2018_AE02: Under-specified theme; exemplar quote ('being without cannabis') suggests withdrawal-type discomfort from facility restriction on another substance rather than a direct ibogaine drug effect, but no intervention/severity detail given. Defaulted to Mild, SeverityIndeterminate=Y.
ae_events.Davis 2018_AE03: This is the most frequently reported challenge theme overall (23% of responder utterances) and is explicitly framed in the Abstract/Discussion as a persisting post-treatment need. The exemplar quote references difficulty spanning 'the 4 weeks after' treatment, which maps to the rubric's Moderate criterion of functional/psychological impairment persisting days-to-weeks beyond the dosing day. Graded Moderate on this duration signal rather than defaulting to Mild; SeverityIndeterminate set to N since a signal (persistence over weeks) was used, though this is inferred from a single exemplar quote rather than a systematic duration report for all 34 responders who endorsed this theme, so the grade carries more uncertainty than a fully-specified event.
ae_events.Davis 2018_AE04: Under-specified theme ('sleeping after treatment'); no duration/intervention signal beyond the label 'Exhaustion/Fatigue'. Defaulted to Mild, SeverityIndeterminate=Y.
ae_events.Davis 2018_AE05: Under-specified theme ('uncomfortable and raw feelings'); no duration/intervention signal. Defaulted to Mild, SeverityIndeterminate=Y. Classified as AE rather than challenging_experience since it reads as a general negative-affect symptom rather than psychedelic-phenomenology processing.
ae_events.Davis 2018_AE06: Under-specified theme ('the restlessness afterward'); no duration/intervention signal. Defaulted to Mild, SeverityIndeterminate=Y.
